Find the $x$-intercepts of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-8x+6y+15=0,$ shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
We must have $y=0$ at the $x$-intercepts. 

So, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-8x+6y+15 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+{0}^{2}-8x+6\cdot 0+15 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-8x+15 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this equation by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-8x+16+15 & =0+16 \\ (x-4)^{2}+15 & =16 \\ (x-4)^{2} & =1 \\ x-4 & =\pm 1 \\ x & =4\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts occur at the points $(3,0)$ and $(5,0).$
